description: RDD2022 is an annotated road-image collection released for the Crowdsensing-based Road Damage Detection Challenge. The public Figshare page reports 47,420 images from Japan, India, the Czech Republic, Norway, the United States and China, with more than 55,000 labelled damage instances. Four classes cover longitudinal cracks, transverse cracks, alligator cracks and potholes. The organiser repository says training images use JPEG files with Pascal VOC XML annotations and that test images are unlabelled. Figshare lists CC BY 4.0 and a public version-one release. The images can train a road-condition detection component for inspection or maintenance-planning simulations. They do not give repeated condition histories, repair costs or traffic loads, so a deterioration model needs additional data. Country and camera differences may affect detection performance, and class labels do not directly measure structural severity. The 12.36 GB package was not downloaded and labels were not checked. No directly related catalogue dataset was identified.
